turns.question: Thinking back to when you were a kid, do you remember having similar problems staying focused or getting easily distracted back then?
How much are these problems with getting pulled off track affecting your performance at work right now—for example, are they causing missed deadlines, errors, or negative feedback from your manager?
These days, do you often feel an inner sense of restlessness, like you’re driven by a motor or can’t relax and sit still for long, even when you want to?
Do you often feel a lot of nervousness or worry in your day-to-day life, even when nothing in particular is going wrong at that moment?
Do you have ongoing trouble falling asleep at night, like your mind won’t shut off and you regularly lie awake much longer than you’d like before actually drifting off?

When you think about conversations or social situations, do you often find it hard to read other people’s cues—like knowing when it’s your turn to talk, whether they’re bored, or what they’re feeling from their tone or expressions?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you often felt noticeably down, sad, or like you’ve lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

In your day-to-day life right now, outside of work—like managing bills, chores, appointments, or personal projects—do your focus and follow-through problems cause you to miss or forget important things often enough that it creates real problems for you?

Back in grade school and high school, did your trouble with focus and getting distracted show up in at least two different places—for example both at school and at home—rather than just in one setting?
When you think back over your life, have you had this kind of trouble staying focused and getting sidetracked since you were a kid, or is it more of a recent change for you?
Lately, do you find yourself feeling worried or tense much of the day, even about things that aren’t immediately going wrong?
Outside of work, do these difficulties with staying focused or getting sidetracked also cause problems for you—for example in managing things like chores, errands, or personal projects?
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down or sad most days, even when nothing in particular has gone wrong?
Right now in your current job, are these focus and follow‑through problems causing you clear trouble with your performance, like missed deadlines or feedback from your manager about reliability?

When you were a kid, did adults ever describe you as unusually restless or "hyper," like having trouble staying seated, always fidgeting, or seeming to be constantly on the go compared with other children?

Thinking about your life right now, do you notice these same focus and follow‑through problems showing up in at least two different parts of your life, like for example both at home and in social or hobby situations?

Right now, when you sit down to do something that requires sustained mental effort—like working on a project or filling out forms—do you often find yourself making careless mistakes or missing details even when you’re genuinely trying to do it carefully?

Thinking back as clearly as you can, were these kinds of focus and follow‑through problems already noticeable in you before you turned 12 years old, rather than only starting later on in your teens or adulthood?
Thinking back to when you were a kid, say in elementary or middle school, do you remember having similar problems staying focused or finishing tasks?
How much are these concentration problems getting in the way of you doing your job or managing day-to-day responsibilities right now?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things—like work, health, money, or relationships—on most days, even when there isn’t an immediate crisis?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day?
How have you been sleeping lately—do you have trouble either falling asleep or staying asleep at night?
Do you often feel physically restless or like you’re driven by a motor—for example, needing to fidget, get up, or move around when you’re supposed to stay seated?
When you think about a typical week recently, how often do you have nights where it takes you a long time to fall asleep or you wake up a lot?
In a usual week, how many nights would you say you have noticeable trouble either falling asleep or staying asleep?
Do you notice these focus and follow-through problems not just with work, but also in other parts of your life, like managing things at home or in your relationships with friends or family?
Thinking back to when you were a kid, say before middle school, do you remember having similar trouble staying focused or getting easily distracted, or is this more of a recent thing as an adult?

These focus and distraction issues you’re describing—do they cause you clear problems in more than one area of your life, for example both at work and also in things like home responsibilities, hobbies, or relationships?
Outside of the distraction and follow-through issues, do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, in a way that feels hard to control or switch off?

In the past few months, have you had periods lasting at least a couple of weeks where you felt on edge or keyed up most days, like your body and mind just wouldn’t settle even when nothing specific was happening right then?

When you get that restless, keyed‑up feeling, is it usually because you’re actively worrying about something bad that might happen, or does it also show up when you’re not particularly worried and are just bored or stuck doing something uninteresting?

When you’re doing something you actually find really interesting or fun, like a favorite hobby or a project you’re excited about, do you still find your mind drifting off or your body feeling restless, or does that mostly happen only with boring or routine tasks?
Over the past month, have you often felt down, depressed, or like you’ve lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
Lately, have you been having trouble either falling asleep at night or staying asleep through the night often enough that it feels like a real problem for you?

When you’re doing something you genuinely find interesting or fun, like a hobby or a project you’re really into, do you still often lose track of what you’re doing because your attention jumps to other thoughts or distractions?

Thinking back to when you were a kid in elementary or middle school, did you often have similar trouble staying focused on schoolwork or instructions, even for things you were trying to pay attention to?
These attention problems you’re describing now—do they significantly get in the way of your day-to-day functioning in more than one area of your life, like at work, at home, or in relationships?
Over the past few months, have you been feeling excessively worried or tense on most days, even when nothing specific is going wrong?
Over the last few weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticeably less interested or less motivated to do things than is usual for you?

Outside of being talkative or interrupting, have you generally found it hard to understand or keep up with social cues—like reading people’s expressions, knowing when someone is bored or joking, or figuring out what’s expected in conversations?
Do you often have trouble falling asleep at night, taking a long time to drift off even when you’re trying to sleep?

In situations where you’re expected to sit still or stay put—like meetings, classes in the past, or long conversations—do you often feel physically restless or find yourself fidgeting, getting up, or feeling like you’re driven by a motor?

When you’re doing something you genuinely enjoy and find really interesting—like a favorite hobby, game, or show—do you still often find your attention slipping away or feel that same restless, driven feeling in your body?
Over the past month, have you had trouble falling asleep on at least three nights most weeks?
Outside of these tracking concerns, do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people don’t seem to hear?
When people you trust tell you that this is just normal oversight and not personal, how convinced do you still feel that dispatch and the other drivers are specifically watching and reporting on you?
If you discovered clear proof that dispatch and the other drivers were not tracking you personally after all, how willing do you think you’d be to change your mind about this?
Have you ever seen things that other people don’t seem to see, like shadows, figures, or movements that you later couldn’t explain?

Aside from the work tracking systems that everyone knows about, do you feel absolutely certain that dispatch and the other drivers are secretly and specifically targeting you in a way that most people would find hard to believe?
Apart from the situation with dispatch and the other drivers, do you currently have any other strong beliefs that people around you say are strange or hard to believe?
Do you know other people in your workplace or community who share this same belief that dispatch and the drivers are secretly targeting specific workers the way you feel they are targeting you?
How long have you been feeling that dispatch and the other drivers are specifically watching and reporting on you like this?
How anxious or on edge do you feel in your day-to-day life because of this situation with dispatch and the other drivers?

When you think about dispatch tracking your route changes and other drivers reporting on you, do you feel completely certain this is really happening, or do you see it as more of a worry that might be mistaken?
Have any supervisors or coworkers ever directly told you that they are tracking you or reporting on you, or is this something you’ve concluded from how things seem to line up?
Aside from the situation with dispatch and the other drivers, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things in your life, to the point that it feels hard to control the worrying?
When you step back from the situation and really think it through, do you feel it is actually possible that you might be misinterpreting what’s happening with dispatch and the other drivers?
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you didn’t seem to hear, when there wasn’t a clear source for them?
Has this sense that dispatch and other drivers are tracking or reporting on you led to any concrete problems at work, like write-ups, conflicts, or trouble doing your job?

When people you trust, like your husband or close friends, hear your concerns about dispatch and the other drivers, do you still feel sure that your explanation is right, or do their reactions ever seriously make you doubt that this is really happening?
Over the past month, has this situation at work been making you feel stressed or on edge almost every day, even when you’re not actually at work?
Because of your sense that dispatch and the other drivers are tracking or reporting on you, have you actually avoided going in to work or called out when you otherwise wouldn’t have?
Do you ever feel that people at work are secretly trying to harm you or set you up, beyond just watching your performance?

When friends or family tell you this is just normal oversight and not people targeting you, do you ever find yourself thinking they might be right, or are you completely sure your coworkers are reporting on you?
Have you ever heard voices or sounds, or seen things, that other people around you don’t seem to hear or see?
Aside from the tracking system and radio, do you ever feel that people outside of work—like strangers in public places—are also watching you or talking about you in some special way?

If your manager showed you clear proof that the tracking and radio comments were just routine and not about you personally, how likely is it that you would believe them and let go of the idea that certain drivers are reporting on you?
Because of your belief that certain drivers are reporting on you, have you actually changed how you behave at work—for example, avoiding people, routes, or the radio—more than you normally would?
Over the past couple of weeks, how has your mood been overall—have you been feeling down or depressed more days than not?
When you think about the idea that certain drivers are reporting on you, do you feel absolutely sure this is true, or do you still have real doubts that it might be a misunderstanding?
Do you ever feel that your thoughts, actions, or feelings are being controlled or influenced by someone or something outside of you?

When you notice these patterns and comments, do you ever find yourself wondering if you might be misinterpreting things, or are you completely certain that people are definitely tracking and reporting on you?
Aside from these patterns and comments from coworkers, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people don’t seem to hear?

If someone you really trusted showed you clear proof that dispatch and the other drivers weren’t actually coordinating or reporting on you, how likely is it that you would change your mind about this?
Outside of what’s happening at work, do you have any other strong beliefs that you feel sure are true but that other people say are strange or hard to believe?
Do you ever feel like your thoughts, actions, or movements are being controlled or influenced by someone or something outside of you, rather than fully coming from you yourself?
Do you ever feel as if other people can somehow hear your thoughts or know exactly what you are thinking, even when you haven’t said anything out loud?
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energized or upbeat, needed much less sleep than usual, and were more active or driven than is typical for you?
How much have these worries about dispatch and the other drivers been affecting your day-to-day life, for example your ability to work, relax, or enjoy things outside of work?
Has there ever been a moment, even briefly, when you thought to yourself, "Maybe I’m wrong about them coordinating and reporting on me"?
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you don’t seem to hear, when there’s no radio or other obvious source?
When you think about dispatch and the other drivers watching and commenting on you, how sure are you that this is really happening, on a scale from 0 to 100 percent?
In the past few weeks, have you been feeling noticeably down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

When someone you trust suggests that these things at work might be coincidences or misunderstandings, are you ever able to seriously consider that possibility, even briefly, or does it still feel definitely true to you no matter what they say?
Outside of your job, do you ever feel that people in other places—like neighbors, stores, or in public—are also watching you or sending you hidden messages about you?

Because of these concerns about dispatch and the other drivers, have you actually changed your behavior in any clear way—like avoiding certain routes, refusing assignments, or confronting people about it?

When you think specifically about the idea that dispatch and certain drivers are tracking and reporting on you, how distressing does that belief feel to you in the moment, on a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 is not upsetting at all and 10 is the most upset you can imagine?

Before this situation at work started, have you ever had a period in your life when you were clearly out of touch with reality—like being convinced of something others said was impossible, or needing hospital care because of your thoughts or perceptions?

Right now, as you’re sitting here with me, if you focus just on the idea that dispatch and certain drivers are tracking and reporting on you, does that feel absolutely true to you, or does any part of you currently feel unsure that it’s really happening?
When you’re rechecking things like locks or your notes, do you feel at some level that the amount of checking you’re doing is excessive or unreasonable, or does it feel completely necessary to you?

Aside from the checking itself, do you get intrusive thoughts or mental images that pop into your mind against your will and feel distressing or senseless, which you then try to neutralize or relieve by checking?
On a typical day, roughly how much total time do you spend on these checking routines, from when they start until you can finally move on?
Because of all this checking, what in your life has actually been affected the most—like your work, studies, relationships, or daily routine?

Outside of those specific checking situations, do you also tend to feel worried or tense about lots of different everyday things most of the day, even when you’re not in the middle of a checking routine?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or noticeably sad most days, even when you’re not caught up in the checking?
Right before you start checking, do you usually get any intrusive, unwanted thoughts or mental images about something bad happening if you don’t check, that feel hard to dismiss?

How much are these checking routines and the anxiety around them actually getting in the way of your day-to-day life—for example, making you late, interfering with work, or stopping you from doing things you want to do?
Outside of these specific checking situations, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worrying excessively about lots of different everyday things, even when nothing in particular has gone wrong?
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down or sad most of the day on most days, even at times when you’re not caught up in the checking or anxiety about mistakes?

When you catch yourself going back to re-check things, does any part of you feel like, "This is over the top and doesn’t really make sense, but I still feel driven to do it," or does it mostly feel like the careful and correct way to do things?
Right before you start checking things, what kinds of thoughts or fears are going through your mind, if any?

When you’re doing these checking routines, do you feel deep down that the amount of checking you’re doing is excessive or doesn’t really make sense, or does it mostly feel reasonable and necessary to you?
Do these checking routines always come after a specific, unwanted thought or image popping into your mind, or do you more often just feel a general worry or tension that makes you check things a lot?
Over a typical week, about how much time per day do you spend caught up in these checking routines, from when they start until you’re finally able to move on?
Because of these checking routines and the anxiety around them, have you actually been missing deadlines, making mistakes at work, or having problems in your relationships or daily responsibilities?

Outside of those moments when a specific “what if I missed something and someone gets hurt” thought suddenly pops in, do you also spend a lot of your day feeling generally worried or tense about many different things, even when you’re not checking anything?

On days when nothing in particular has triggered your checking, do you still find yourself worrying a lot about different things like health, money, work, or family for much of the day, or are you mostly okay until a specific checking-type thought pops up?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling noticeably more down or unable to enjoy things most of the day, nearly every day?

When you feel the need to recheck things, is it because you get specific, intrusive thoughts or images that something bad will happen if you don’t do it a certain way, even though you know they don’t really make sense?
Because of this rechecking and the anxiety around it, how much is it actually interfering with your day-to-day life—for example, making you late, hurting your work, or affecting your relationships?
When you get stuck rechecking, in that moment do you feel like the level of checking you’re doing is clearly excessive or unreasonable, or does it mostly feel justified to you?

Outside of these specific situations where you’re rechecking things, do you also find yourself worrying a lot about many different everyday things—like money, health, work performance, or family—most days, even when nothing in particular has gone wrong?

Apart from physically rechecking things, do you also find yourself doing mental rituals—like repeatedly going over events, numbers, or phrases in your head in a very specific way—to try to feel less anxious or prevent something bad from happening?
How long have you been having these rechecking routines and feeling like you can’t move on until they feel “right”?
Thinking back, would you say these rechecking routines have been going on for at least a year, or has it been less than a year so far?

When you try to resist or cut short the checking routines—for example, deciding you will check something only once and then stop—does your anxiety or discomfort quickly build up to the point that it feels almost impossible not to go back and check again?

Outside of the moments when you’re actively checking things, do you ever get sudden, unwanted thoughts or images about something terrible happening that pop into your mind and feel intrusive, like they don’t fit with what you actually want or believe?

When you feel you have to recheck things, is it usually because you’re getting intrusive, unwanted thoughts or mental images about something bad happening if you don’t, or is it more just a general sense of unease?
When these doubts and ‘what if’ thoughts pop up, do you feel, at least part of you, that they’re excessive or don’t really make sense, or do they seem completely reasonable to you in the moment?

When these checking thoughts show up, do they feel like unwanted intrusions that don’t really fit with how you want to think, or do they feel more like your normal way of worrying about things, just stronger than usual?
On a typical day, roughly how much total time do you spend doing these checking routines before you can move on to other things?

Apart from this repeated checking of things, do you have any other recurring, unwanted thoughts or rituals—like needing to wash in a particular way, arrange things symmetrically, repeat certain actions, or mentally go over phrases or numbers—that you feel driven to do to relieve anxiety?
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even when you’re not actively dealing with the checking?

Outside of these checking situations, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about lots of other everyday things, like finances, health, family, or work in general, even when there’s nothing specific to trigger it?

Because of this checking and rechecking, have you actually been missing deadlines, getting in trouble at work, or having problems in your relationships or daily life that wouldn’t be happening otherwise?

Thinking back to before these checking problems became this intense, would you say you’ve always been a very perfectionistic, rigid, rule‑bound person in most areas of life, or did this way of needing things to be just right really start only with the checking getting worse recently?
